name: John Ball
role: Itinerant Kentish priest and radical preacher
description: A Kentish priest with a documented preaching career of radical, egalitarian sermons stretching back at least to the 1360s -- well before John Wycliffe's Lollard movement began attracting attention -- for which he was repeatedly excommunicated and imprisoned by Archbishop Simon Sudbury. Hostile chroniclers later linked him to Wycliffe and the Lollards, a connection modern historians treat with real skepticism: the timeline doesn't support Ball as a Wycliffe follower, and the association looks like a polemical move to discredit both men by association rather than a documented doctrinal link. Freed from Archbishop's prison at Maidstone when the Kentish rebels broke it open in early June 1381 (chroniclers differ on whether he was already at liberty or was released by the crowd). Preached to the assembled rebels at Blackheath on 12 June; later tradition attributes to this sermon the rhyming couplet 'When Adam delved and Eve span, who was then the gentleman?' though the earliest surviving text of the full sermon is a later chronicler's reconstruction rather than a verbatim transcript taken on the day. Captured at Coventry after the revolt collapsed, tried at St Albans, and executed -- hanged, drawn, and quartered -- on 15 July 1381, reportedly in Richard II's presence.
narrative_function: The revolt's ideological voice; the figure whose sermon supplies its enduring rhetorical legacy.
